active_paradigms.idea: Smooth LogSumExp global optimization with analytic gradients via scipy.optimize.minimize (L-BFGS-B)
active_paradigms.description: Replace the coordinate-descent hill climbing with a true gradient-based continuous optimization. The objective min over 286 triangle areas is non-smooth, but a soft-min surrogate like -tau*log(sum(exp(-area_i/tau))) is smooth and differentiable, and the gradient of each triangle area w.r.t. its three vertices has a simple closed form (perpendicular directions). Use scipy.optimize.minimize with method='L-BFGS-B' (or SLSQP) on the 26 variables, maximizing the soft-min. Use a continuation homotopy: start with tau large (averaging many triangles) and progressively shrink tau toward ~1e-4 so the surrogate concentrates on the smallest triangles, re-minimizing at each stage. Run from the current best configuration and a few structured starts, keeping the best true min-area result. This escapes the plateau problem that stalls single-vertex hill climbing because gradients jointly move all points that affect the bottleneck triangles.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized (primary); also reduces eval_time vs many local-search iterations
active_paradigms.cautions: Implement the soft-min gradient analytically in numpy (vectorized over the 286 index triples) rather than finite differences to keep it fast and accurate. Clamp tau from below (~1e-5) to avoid numerical overflow in exp; use area_i/tau with max-subtraction trick. Verify the true min area after each tau stage since the surrogate can drift; keep the best true-min configuration. Keep points inside the unit square via L-BFGS-B bounds.

active_paradigms.idea: Optimize the convex hull shape too: parametrize the region as a stretched/affine-transformed domain instead of fixing the unit square
active_paradigms.description: The metric divides by the convex hull area of the points, not a fixed region — so the shape of the point set's own hull matters. Configurations on a long thin hull have small hull area but also small triangles; the current program clips points to the unit square, which may not be the best hull shape. Instead, optimize points freely in a larger box and let the hull be whatever it is, or explicitly try affine-stretched initial configurations (e.g., points on an elongated hexagon, a triangle-shaped hull, or a regular 13-gon hull). Since Heilbronn-type optimal configurations for small n often place most points on the boundary of a convex polygon, seed starts with 11-13 points on a convex polygon boundary (regular 13-gon, regular 12-gon + center, triangle with points distributed on its three edges) and refine. After optimization, optionally apply a global affine transformation to reduce hull area while scaling all triangle areas proportionally — the normalized score is affine-invariant per-triangle only if hull scales identically, so instead directly check whether shrinking the hull (moving hull vertices inward along normals while keeping interior points fixed relative) increases the ratio.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized by jointly improving the numerator (triangle areas) and denominator (hull area)
active_paradigms.cautions: The normalized ratio is NOT affine-invariant: anisotropic scaling changes triangle areas and hull area by the same determinant factor, so pure area-preserving linear maps leave the score unchanged — the gain comes from nonlinear repositioning (moving hull vertices inward creates slack for interior triangles). Avoid degenerate hulls (collinear hull vertices give zero hull area but also zero min triangle area). Always recompute the true ratio with scipy.spatial.ConvexHull after refinement.

active_paradigms.idea: Simulated annealing / basin-hopping global search with move types matched to Heilbronn geometry
active_paradigms.description: The current multi-start local search gets trapped in local optima of a highly non-convex landscape with ~C(13,3) competing constraints. Use scipy.optimize.basin_hopping (or a hand-rolled deterministic simulated annealing with a fixed seed) over the 26 coordinates with the true min-area as the energy. Design the perturbation step to be geometry-aware: (a) move a random vertex of the current smallest triangle, (b) apply a small random affine jitter to a symmetry group of points, (c) swap an interior point with a boundary point. Use an acceptance temperature schedule that anneals from accepting ~30% worsening moves down to near-zero, with several hundred iterations per start. Combine with the existing greedy polish as the local-minimizer callback so each basin-hopping step lands on a locally refined configuration. This explores fundamentally different basins than the 10 fixed structured starts.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized via better global exploration; combined_score above 1.0
active_paradigms.cautions: Keep everything deterministic: use numpy.random.default_rng with fixed seeds, not scipy's global RNG. Runtime is secondary but must stay within the evaluation timeout — budget iterations (e.g., 200 hops x 5 starts) and vectorize the 286-triangle area computation. The energy (true min area) is piecewise linear and flat in many directions, so pair annealing with the fine-grained polish to escape flat plateaus. Track the best-ever configuration separately from the annealing state.
